name: Dollar funding stress
summary: Fed overnight repo operations jump to $22.8bn in the latest reading to 27 Nov, above the $15bn Watch line
state: Fed overnight repo operations reached $22.75bn in the latest FRED reading to 27 Nov, up from near zero on every day of the previous weeks and above the $15bn Watch line (FRED). SOFR was 3.95% on 25 Nov, 5bp above the Fed's 3.90% interest on reserves, inside the 10bp line (FRED). No use of emergency Fed facilities was found, so the status rises to Watch, not Alert.
for_you: Short-term dollar funding has tightened. Banks, money funds and leveraged investors that rely on overnight borrowing are most exposed; such spikes often cluster around month-end and can fade within days.
rubric_hit: Fed repo ops $22.8bn in $15–50bn Watch band
basis_detail: SOFR–IORB 5d max bp=5.00; Fed repo ops 5d max $bn=22.75

sources.title: FRED — Overnight repurchase agreements: Treasury securities purchased by the Fed (RPONTSYD)

why: Overnight dollar funding is the plumbing of global finance; repo-rate spikes came before the market seizures of September 2019 and March 2020.
drivers: Bank reserves, Treasury issuance and cash balances, quarter-end window dressing, Fed balance-sheet policy.

rubric.alert: SOFR more than 25bp above IORB, or Fed repo operations above $50bn in a day, or emergency Fed liquidity facilities.
rubric.watch: SOFR 10–25bp above IORB on any day in the past week (the top ~10% of weeks since 2024), or Fed repo operations of $15–50bn in a day.
rubric.normal: SOFR less than 10bp above the Fed's interest on reserves (IORB) on every day of the past week, and Fed repo operations under $15bn.
